# fishbowl-jev-ultrafast

> A sandboxed Linux desktop (Debian 12, 1280x800, Chromium, shell; Lima VM on macOS/Linux, WSL2 on Windows), exposed to AI agents as an MCP
> server (stdio) with 25 tools. A human watches live in the browser (noVNC), can pause, and takes over for logins via
> `handoff`. Optional fast mode: a big model plans, Jev (TypeSafe) executes each browser action as multiple-choice
> questions. Command: `fishbowl`. Python package source: https://github.com/ericwang915/fishbowl

## How an agent should use it

- Screen coordinates from `browser_elements` are only valid until the page changes; read them again after an action.
- Prefer `browser_elements` + `browser_click` / `browser_type` / `browser_select` over pixel clicks; use `computer` only outside the browser.
- For multi-step web tasks, call `browser_run` with a `plan` ([{"goal": ..., "text": ...}]). Only `text` from the plan is typed. On `handback`, read `reason`, `log` and `observation`, fix the plan, continue.
- If `browser_run` returns `fast_mode_off`, there is no Jev key: drive step by step with the `browser_*` tools.
- Logins, captchas, 2FA: call `handoff(reason)` and wait. Never ask for passwords in chat.
- `needs_approval`: ask the user in plain words; retry with `approved=true` only after an explicit yes.
- `paused`: stop and wait. Files for the user go in `/workspace` (= `~/vc/workspace` on the Mac).
